summary:
Sheikh Ali Mashhour delivers a Quranic tafseer of Surat Al-Anbiya, focusing on the concept of shirk (associating partners with Allah) and specifically addressing the claim that Allah has children. The lecture traces the historical roots of this concept across various pagan civilizations (Egyptian, Persian, Roman) and discusses how the idea of merging the divine with creation is not unique to Christianity but a recurring human tendency when people worship other than Allah. The sheikh explains the logical progression of thought that leads to such beliefs.

The lecture also addresses the nature of angels in Islamic theology, emphasizing that angels possess free will and the ability to disobey Allah, which is why their obedience is praiseworthy. Sheikh Mashhour clarifies the Islamic concept of intercession (shafaa'ah), distinguishing between the invalid intercession that idolaters believed in (intercession forced upon Allah) and the valid intercession affirmed in the Quran (conditional intercession based on Allah's pleasure with both the intercessor and the one being interceded for).
